column3: Gender affirming care is healthcare, and a human right. Hospitals like Rush and Lurie are caving to far right pressure. Join the us Thursday, July 17th, at 6:00 PM at 523 S Honore to demand gender affirming care for all! \n  \n RSVP: tinyurl.com/rushrally

Lurie Children’s and Rush, two major Chicago area hospitals, are preemptively complying with the Trump administration’s attacks on trans people and rolling back gender affirming care for trans youth. (1/8)
By doing so, these hospitals defy state laws such as the IL HRA and are consciously denying life-saving surgeries to minors, betraying patient care and community trust. (2/8)

Chicago Democratic Socialists of America worked with our allies in the Chicago City Council to introduce a resolution  (R2025-0018757) this week condemning Rush Hospital and Lurie Children’s Hospital for ceasing gender-affirming care. (full reso: chicityclerkelms.chicago.gov/Matter/?matt...) (3/8)

We want to thank 26th Ward Alder Jesse Fuentes, who introduced the resolution, and socialist in office and 33rd Ward Alder Rossana Rodríguez-Sánchez whose office worked closely with Chicago DSA members to craft this resolution. (4/8)
In times of political repression and advances by the Far Right, we need bold leadership. Socialists and their allies in office are rising to the occasion. (5/8)
The Trump administration wants to eliminate gender affirming care in this country by punishing providers and holding patients hostage in order to push their radical reactionary agenda. (6/8)

But this is Chicago.  
 We don't bow to bullies. 
  
 As socialists we believe in fighting the boss head on. Trans liberation won’t be won through closed door negotiation but through mass action by ordinary working class people. (7/8)

What you can do? Call your Alder and voice your support for resolution: R2025-0018757 and join us for a rally to fight for trans youth near Rush hospital at 6PM @ Louis Pasteur Statue | 523 S Honore  tinyurl.com/rushrally (8/8)

If the tax had remained in place, our city would have gained more than $50 million to fund schools, parks, libraries, and safe streets.  \n  \n #corporateheadtax

We honor the life, work, and legacy of the Rev. Jesse Jackson.  \n  \n We acknowledge his work organizing in Chicago during Operation Breadbasket, Operation PUSH, and the Rainbow Coalition as crucial moments in our city’s history for the rights of working Black people and for the broad working class.

We believe his Presidential campaigns in 1984 and 1988 forced the Democratic Party to acknowledge the existence of a Left, multi-racial working class movement, that rejected austerity and racially motivated smears by the Right to divide the working class.

In celebration of Black History Month & the vision of a united multi-racial working class, we encourage everyone to attend the Multi Racial Organizing Committee Social this Saturday, Feb 21st, 6-7:30pm at the Fine Arts Building downtown where we will discuss our mission. \n  \n teamup.com/ksc3uaa38o41...

If you don't know already, our comrade and member Byron Sigcho-Lopez is running for Congress in the Il-4th as an independent Democratic Socialist.

He is doing so after outgoing Congressman Chuy Garcia announced his retirement only hours before the filing deadline to run in the Democratic primary clearing the way for his chief of staff, Patty Garcia, to be the only candidate.
As socialists we cannot tolerate undemocratic maneuvers like this in our city. The party duopoly has erected a lot of legal barriers to independent runs.

Most crucially, our run requires 11k signatures (after our opponents will get ~25% of them thrown out) to get on the ballot. Our chapter has committed to collect 11k signatures on its own while thousands more will come from community allies.
Getting on the ballot is going to be a very close call. Sign up TODAY for a canvassing shift! \n  \n tinyurl.com/volunteerbyron
